I
t is well recognized that quaternary carbon centres exist widely 
in natural products, bioactive compounds and drugs (Fig. 1a). 
When the four substituents are different, a quaternary carbon 
stereogenic centre is generated. Because of the resultant increased 
diversity and conformational constraint, the creation of such a cen
-
tre is of great relevance to the fields of bioscience and medicinal 
chemistry. However, the asymmetric construction of such quater
-
nary carbon centres remains a challenge and of high current scien -
tific and practical importance 1,2. Allenes, meanwhile, have unique 
properties when compared to alkenes and alkynes due to their 
intrinsic three-carbon axial chirality. They have been found in natu
-
ral and non-natural bioactive molecules3 as well as functional mate-
rials4, and are considered to be versatile building blocks, ligands and 
catalysts for organic synthesis5–15.
Recently, much effort has been devoted to the generation of 
this unique linear axial chirality 16–25. Optically active tetrasubsti -
tuted allenes are of fundamental interest, providing an alternative 
approach to creating the challenging and very important chiral qua
-
ternary carbon centres (up to three) (Fig. 1b) 1,2, but it is still chal -
lenging to access these allenes 26–30. Although asymmetric addition 
to (di)cyclohexenynones, as developed by Hayashi31, Sun32 and their 
colleagues (Fig. 1c), and the enantioselective trapping of some rather 
specific allenyl anions with different electrophiles, as developed by 
Maruoka
33, Miller 34, Feng/Liu 35,36 and List 37, have been reported 
(Fig. 1d), racemic propargylic alcohols, a class of very common 
chemicals, would, in principle, be the most straightforward starting 
point to creating optically active tetrasubstituted allenes (Fig. 1e). 
However, no such protocol has been reported, hinting that tradi
-
tional catalysts may not work for this purpose.
Here, we report our developments in this area—efficient metal-
catalysed successive kinetic resolutions for the synthesis of both 
enantiomers of tetrasubstituted 2,3-allenoic acids 33,37 from readily 
available racemic tertiary propargylic alcohols by applying a com -
mercially available chiral ligand, DTBM-SEGphos, with Brønsted 
acid, forming a transient leaving group (Fig. 1f). The key here is the 
addition of PPh3 as the supporting ligand. These synthetically ver -
satile allenoic acid products may be easily converted to other use -
ful functionalized allenes and cyclic compounds with a quaternary 
carbon stereogenic centre
5,7,10,12–14.
Results
Optimization of reaction conditions. We initiated the study by the 
traditional strategy of screening various commercially available chi
-
ral ligands for the asymmetric carboxylation reaction of 2-pheny -
loct-3-yn-2-ol 1a with (PhO) 2POOH to form a transient leaving 
group (for details see Supplementary Fig. 1 and equation (1)). After 
screening nearly all different types of commercially available ligands 
with different reaction parameters, as expected we identified that 
(R)-DTBM-SEGphos was the best ligand, affording (R)-2a in 38% 
yield with merely 33% e.e. and a 42% yield of achiral 2,4-dienoic 
acid (E)-2a′ (Table 1, entry 3). We then found that the addition of 
supporting ligand, PPh
3, led to a dramatic and unexpected enhance-
ment in enantioselectivity (42% yield, 80% e.e., Table 1, entry 4), 
and only 3% yield of by-product (E)-2a′. As a comparison, when 
6 mol% of supporting ligand PPh
3 was added with (R)-SEGphos, 
the enantioselectivity was also improved to 16% from 3% (Table 1, 
entries 1 and 2).
We next conducted an extensive optimization of the reaction 
conditions to improve the e.e. for the formation of allenoic acid 
(R)-2a (for details see Supplementary Tables 1–5). The enanti
-
oselectivity was improved to 85% by increasing the loading of 
water to 20 equiv. and PPh
3 to 20 mol% (Supplementary Table 1, 
entry 1). (PhO) 2POOH was found to be most efficient in activat -
ing the hydroxyl group after examining different Brønsted acids 
T etrasubstituted allenes via the palladium-
catalysed kinetic resolution of propargylic 
alcohols using a supporting ligand
Wei-Feng Zheng1, Wanli Zhang1, Chaofan Huang1, Penglin Wu1, Hui Qian   1*, Lei Wang2, 
Yin-Long Guo2* and Shengming Ma   1,2*
Efficient enantioselective construction of fully substituted allenes from simple starting materials is still a fundamental chal-
lenge due to the difficulty to discriminate between the four substituents at the 1- and 3-positions of the three-carbon axis of 
chirality. Here, we report a straightforward catalytic asymmetric synthesis of tetrasubstituted 2,3-allenoic acids from readily 
available racemic propargylic alcohols. Enabled by the co-catalysis of palladium and a Brønsted acid in the presence of a com-
mercially available chiral ligand (DTBM-SEGphos) and an achiral monophosphine supporting ligand (PPh
3), the kinetic resolu-
tion of propargylic alcohols proceeded efficiently in the presence of water and 1 atm CO, affording tetrasubstituted 2,3-allenoic 
acids in excellent enantioselectivity and atom economy with a good functional group compatibility. Performing a second kinetic 
resolution on the unreacted alcohol gave access to the other enantiomer of the product. These allenes are precursors to com-
pounds with quaternary carbon centres and other chiral tetrasubstituted allene building blocks, which are of great interest.

20 mol% of (PhO)2POOH, 20 mol% of PPh3 and 20 equiv. of H2O in 
toluene at −5 °C under 1 atm of CO (Supplementary Table 1, entry 
16), affording the desired allenoic acid (R)-2a in 41% NMR yield 
with 94% e.e.
Substrate scope. With the optimized conditions, we next exam -
ined the scope of this straightforward approach for chiral 2,3-alle -
noic acid synthesis. As shown in Fig. 2, a variety of racemic tertiary 
propargylic alcohols bearing electron-neutral, electron-rich and 
electron-deficient aryl moieties all smoothly underwent this trans
-
formation, forming tetrasubstituted chiral 2,3-allenoic acids ((S)-2a 
to (S)-2j) in good yields with over 90% e.e. Steric hindrance slightly 
affects the enantioselectivity because the e.e. for the substrates 
bearing the methyl group at the o-, m- and p-positions decreased 
in order from (S)-2b to ( S)-2d. It is worth noting that when R

To further demonstrate the potential of this protocol, we car -
ried out the gram-scale successive kinetic resolution of propargylic 
alcohols for the synthesis of both enantiomers of chiral 2,3-allenoic 
acid 2 (Fig. 3a). When 10.0 mmol of (±)-1a was submitted to the 
standard conditions with (R)-DTBM-SEGphos as ligand, 0.8529 g 
(37% yield) of (S)-2a with 93% e.e. was isolated (Fig. 3a, entry 1). 
All the recovered (S)-1a in 63% e.e. was subsequently subjected to 
the standard conditions, again with the enantiomer (S)-DTBM-
SEGphos as ligand, to give 0.8172 g (71% yield) of the enantiomer 
(R)-2a with 98% e.e. Successive kinetic resolution of other racemic 
propargylic alcohols, such as (±)-1y, (±)-1f and all alkyl substituted 
(±)-1k, showed that all were efficiently realized to afford both enan
-
tiomers (Fig. 3a, entries 2–4). To demonstrate the practicality of this 
approach further, a 50 mmol scale successive kinetic resolution of 
(±)-1a was conducted, affording 5.1 g of (S)-2a and 4.3 g of (R)-2a 
(Fig. 3a, entry 5).

2,3-allenoic acid products have been demonstrated by providing 
efficient chirality transfer-based protocols to afford optically active 
compounds with the challenging quaternary chiral carbon centres 
(Fig. 3b). A cyclization reaction of (R)-2a catalysed by CuCl pro
-
ceeded smoothly, affording 2(5H)-furanone (S)-3 in 95% yield with 
98% e.e.
38. The bromolactonization of (R)-2a to 4-bromo-2(5H)-
furanone (R)-4 (96% yield, 98% e.e.) was successfully realized in 
the presence of NBS. With PdCl
2 as catalyst, the allylated buteno -
lide (R)-5 can be effectively assembled in 83% yield with 97% e.e.39. 
4-(1′,3′-Dien-2′-yl)-2(5H)-furanone derivative (R)-6 was formed 
with excellent chirality transfer via PdCl
2-catalysed cross-coupling 
cyclization of (R)-2a with 2,3-allenols 40. The synthetically versatile 
tetrasubstituted 2,3-allenol (R)-7 was easily prepared by esterifica -
tion followed by reduction with DIBAL-H at −78 °C (Fig. 3b).
Mechanistic studies. Kinetic studies revealed a first-order depen -
dence of the reaction rate with respect to substrate 1a (ν = k·[1a]) 
([1a] is the concentration of substrate 1a at time t) (Fig. 4a; for details 
see Supplementary Tables 9 and 10). Furthermore, when submit -
ting optically active (R)-1a and (S)-1a to the same optimal reaction  
conditions, separately, (R)-1a was smoothly converted to the alle -
noic acid (S)-2a; however, the reaction of (S)-1a was extremely 
sluggish (Fig. 4b; for details see Supplementary Tables 11 and 12), 
offering an easy-to-handle protocol for the successive kinetic reso

lution shown in Fig. 3a.

is different from the reaction conducted at 50 °C shown in entry 4 
of Table 1. In addition, the e.e. of the recovered (S)-1a was higher in 
the reaction with PPh3 (Fig. 4f).

Conclusions
In summary, we have realized the efficient catalytic asymmetric 
formation of tetrasubstituted 2,3-allenoic acids from very com
-
mon racemic propargylic alcohols. Enabled by the co-catalysis of 
palladium and a Brønsted acid, the successive kinetic resolution 
reaction of propargylic alcohols proceeded efficiently under 1 atm 
CO and water with a very decent functional group compatibility, 
affording both enantiomers of these tetrasubstituted 2,3-allenoic 
acids in excellent enantioselectivity and atom economy. The pres
-
ence of PPh3 as a supporting ligand is critical for this protocol and 
such a strategy may also work in other metal-catalysed asymmetric 
catalysis. Such chiral 2,3-allenoic acids are very useful in organic 
chemistry. Further studies in this area, including investigation of 
the working mechanism for PPh
3, are being actively pursued in  
this laboratory.
